target_customer: Students and families in Indonesia and the Philippines paying tuition by installments, plus partner schools and lenders who use its platform
problem: University students in Southeast Asia lacked affordable ways to pay tuition and had no credit history; alternatives were family help, informal payday lenders or traditional banks.
business_model: Consumer education financing (interest or fees on installment plans) with later B2B school software and servicing; brands Danacita and Bukas

founders.name: Naga Tan
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as CEO and co-founder. No background found.

founders.name: Susli Lie
founders.background_notes: YC page says she grew up in Indonesia, was first in her family at university, holds degrees from Yale, Wharton and Johns Hopkins, and is now a Partner at Monk's Hill Ventures. Degree types not stated.

competitors.name: Cicil
competitors.what: Indonesian tuition installment fintech for students
competitors.funding_then: Series A led by East Ventures and Vertex Ventures in August 2018, total about 5 million dollars

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit underwriting for thin-file students, collections and school integrations; standard fintech engineering with risk modeling.

defensibility.rationale: School partnerships and lending licenses and funding lines are slow to replicate, but several rivals offered similar installment plans.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the niche; rival Pintek's education product reportedly closed and KoinWorks closed its education product per DailySocial.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2021) describes students relying on family, payday lenders and banks; Indonesian rivals such as Cicil raised money in 2018, which shows investor and student demand for tuition installments.

branding.domain_note: Uses erudifi.com; consumer brands Danacita and Bukas run separate local identities.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission language about making education affordable

brand_strength.rationale: Local consumer brands carry the customer relationship while the parent name is B2B; no source shows brand driven growth.

pivots.to: School software (Campus) and AI collections assistant alongside financing
pivots.why: not stated; the company website now describes financial infrastructure for education

outcome_analysis: ErudiFi built tuition financing for Indonesia and the Philippines under local brands, raised a 5 million dollar Series A in February 2021 and a 15 million dollar Helicap debt facility in January 2022, and bought edtech startup Doyobi in 2024 per DealStreetAsia. It claims over 60 million dollars financed and 200 partner schools. It is still active, and competitors in the niche have closed products.
notes: CB Insights shows 20.12M raised over 4 rounds including two rounds not found in sources; unverified and not recorded. Earlier seed money and YC deal not found. Helicap debt amount and date came from a search summary and the press page URL, which was not opened. Doyobi acquisition dated February 2024 from a search summary. Founded year: CB Insights says 2017, not recorded as it is an aggregator.
